description: C++ programs for the Arduino Mega 2560.

lessons.name: 01 Blink LED
lessons.description: Blink the built-in LED on the Arduino Mega.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Arduino Mega 2560:
No external LED is required.

The built-in LED is connected to digital pin 13.

Connect the Mega to the computer using USB and upload the program using Arduino IDE.

lessons.name: 02 Button Input
lessons.description: Read a push button and control the built-in LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg of the button -> Arduino Mega D22
Other leg -> GND

The program uses INPUT_PULLUP, so an external resistor is not required.

Built-in LED -> D13.

lessons.name: 03 Buzzer
lessons.description: Generate a tone using a buzzer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Buzzer:
Positive (+) -> Arduino Mega D24
Negative (-) -> GND

The buzzer produces a 1000 Hz tone for 500 milliseconds.

lessons.name: 04 Traffic Light
lessons.description: Control red, yellow, and green LEDs as a traffic light.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Red LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D22
Cathode (-) -> GND

Yellow LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D23
Cathode (-) -> GND

Green LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> D24
Cathode (-) -> GND.

lessons.name: 05 Serial Monitor
lessons.description: Display messages and analog readings in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
No external components are required.

Connect the Arduino Mega to the computer using USB.

Open Arduino IDE -> Tools -> Serial Monitor.
Set the baud rate to 9600.

lessons.name: 06 Analog Input
lessons.description: Read an analog value from a potentiometer.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Potentiometer:
One outer pin -> 5V
Middle pin -> A0
Other outer pin -> GND

The Arduino Mega reads an analog value from approximately 0 to 1023.

lessons.name: 07 LED Fade
lessons.connectionGuide:
LED:
Anode (+) -> 220 ohm resistor -> Arduino Mega D6
Cathode (-) -> GND

D6 supports PWM and is used to control LED brightness.

lessons.name: 08 Light Sensor
lessons.description: Read an LDR light sensor and automatically control the built-in LED.
lessons.connectionGuide:
LDR circuit:
Use an LDR and a 10K resistor as a voltage divider.

Voltage divider output -> A0

Built-in LED -> D13.

The LED turns ON when the measured light value is below 500.

lessons.name: 09 Button Counter
lessons.description: Count button presses and display the count in Serial Monitor.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> Arduino Mega D22
Other leg -> GND

The internal pull-up resistor is used.

Open Serial Monitor at 9600 baud to view the button count.

lessons.name: 10 Button LED Toggle
lessons.description: Toggle the built-in LED ON and OFF with a push button.
lessons.connectionGuide:
Push Button:
One leg -> Arduino Mega D22
Other leg -> GND

Built-in LED:
Arduino Mega D13

Each press toggles the LED between ON and OFF.
